added_failures_note: the reviewed run records no baseline_suite/after_suite pair: its manifest names one pytest log (gate.log) and no base arm. That log runs to its summary line at revision c752333ed with 24 passed and EXIT=0, so the head arm's failure set is empty and no added failure can exist; the base arm is unmeasured rather than measured zero. The reviewed head 530dab405 changes only the fragment renderer, the regenerated report labels and the SVG, and no suite log was recorded at 530dab405.
after_suite_note: the reviewed manifest names this log as test_logs, not as an after_suite block, and its header revision c752333ed is one commit before the reviewed head 530dab405

findings.text: non-blocking: the property this delta was landed for — an SVG carrying no <text element so no renderer needs a font — has no committed test; the only check is the run-time negative-control-figure.log, so an edit that sets svg.fonttype back to 'none' or restores the hand-written SVG leaves tests/standard_names green while the label-less figure returns.

non-blocking: figure.clear() empties the figure but leaves it registered in pyplot because plt.subplots created it, so every call to render_figure accumulates one more managed figure in a long-lived process; plt.close(figure) releases it instead.

non-blocking: axes.grid(axis='x', color='#eeeeee', linewidth=0.8) keeps six faint full-height vertical gridlines, non-data ink the house plot style leaves out; carried from the figure review of this same head and not repaired by 530dab405.

justifications.durability: no test file in the reviewed run imports or exercises docs/evidence/fragments/sn-case-file-generation/benchmark.py, so nothing in tests/standard_names reddens if render_figure at :1268 returns to a text-element SVG or to svg.fonttype 'none'; the only guard is the run-time check in negative-control-figure.log.
justifications.evidence: the reviewed run's gate.log is the only suite arm recorded and its header names revision c752333ed, one commit before the reviewed head 530dab405, while the head's own evidence is negative-control-figure.log (text_elements 19 EXIT=1 on the pre-fix figure, 0 EXIT=0 on the repaired one) read and independently reproduced here, not a suite run.
justifications.fit: the renderer follows the established evidence-fragment idiom (matplotlib rc_context plus a direct figure save with metadata Date None, as at docs/evidence/fragments/sn-catalog-grouping/scg-jev-tree-benchmark-run.py:383) and introduces no new module-level name beyond the existing render_figure.
justifications.goal_fidelity: docs/evidence/fragments/sn-case-file-generation/benchmark.py:1268-1330 draws the same six arms, intervals and value labels the goal's evidence needs, and the landed SVG at docs/figures/sn-case-file-generation/scfg-benchmark/heldout-arm-right.svg carries the labels as glyph outlines so no renderer can drop them.
justifications.reuse: the repository's checked figure exporter is imas_codex/plotting/style.py:103 save_figure, which declares a slide width and runs text-clipping checks and so does not fit a documentation figure; 33 sibling fragments under docs/evidence save through figure.savefig directly (git grep -l 'savefig(' at 530dab405 lists 34 files including this one), and matplotlib 3.11.2 already defaults svg.fonttype to 'path', so the rc override extends the fragment idiom rather than forking the owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff c752333ed..530dab405 names only the four declared paths, and the report rewrites are the two regenerated labels rather than new figures or prose.

negative_checks.figure_property: independently measured from the committed artifacts: c752333ed:heldout-arm-right.svg carries 19 '<text' elements and 0 DejaVuSans glyph references; 530dab405:heldout-arm-right.svg carries 0 '<text' elements and 310 DejaVuSans glyph references; ImageMagick rasterization of both at 96 dpi shows dark pixels in the title band and the left label column for the head figure.
